nea.wxt: Showers in the north and east
nea.sum: Smoke haze from Sumatra drifted in, pushing the 24-hr PSI just past 100 in one region.
Afternoon showers brought readings down. Heavy cloud cover meant satellites could not fully see the fires or smoke that day.
Showers across Singapore and parts of Sumatra brought one of the lowest PM2.5 readings in NEA's evening updates (11–21 µg/m³). The forecast dropped to Moderate.
The lowest 24-hr PSI in NEA's evening updates in September. Dry weather over southern Sumatra and Kalimantan kept the fires going, but showers nearer Singapore were expected to limit the haze.
A quieter day, but NEA flagged the risk of haze returning with winds forecast from the east-southeast or southeast.
Dense plumes continued over the fire areas. Showers forecast for Singapore were expected to reduce the risk, so the forecast stayed Moderate.
A dry day and moderate to dense haze from Kalimantan drifted in. PM2.5 nearly reached 100 µg/m³ by the evening.

nea.wxt: Heavy showers late morning and afternoon
nea.sum: Heavy showers cleared the air (PM2.5 12–24 µg/m³), but the 24-hr PSI still showed the overnight haze, reaching 119 in central Singapore.

nea.wxt: Brief showers in the north and east
nea.sum: The highest PM2.5 in any of NEA's evening updates in September (138 µg/m³), as dense smoke from southern Sumatra and Kalimantan arrived. NEA forecast the 24-hr PSI would reach the mid Unhealthy range.

For the first time in September every region was Unhealthy at the evening reading, with PSI up to 157, the highest in NEA's updates so far. Smoke kept drifting in from Kalimantan and southern Sumatra.

nea.wxt: Showers over Singapore and the region
nea.sum: Showers brought the lowest PM2.5 in NEA's evening updates in September (6–18 µg/m³), and PSI eased to 91–112. Smoke from southern Sumatra and Kalimantan was still drifting towards Singapore.

nea.title: Outlook for the first half of October
nea.sum: NEA's fortnightly weather outlook: drier than the previous fortnight, winds from the southeast or southwest, thundery showers on some afternoons, and total rainfall below average.

nea.wxt: Showers over several parts of Singapore
nea.sum: Showers kept the air in the Moderate range, with PSI at 60–73. Smoke from southern Kalimantan drifted towards the vicinity of Singapore, and NEA warned that southeasterly or southerly winds could bring more haze.
